title: `CASE`, `IF`, `COALESCE` are lazy; `AND`, `OR` short-circuit left to right; filters can move below projections
verdict: a guarded branch never raises; `b <> 0 AND a div b > 1` is safe, the reverse raises; pushdown only removes raises
description: `CASE WHEN b <> 0 THEN a div b END`, `if(b = 0, NULL, a div b)` and `CASE WHEN c RLIKE '^[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(c AS INT) END` evaluate the guarded expression only on the rows that reach it, under ANSI too, also when the same subexpression appears twice in a branch or in two `CASE`s (common subexpression elimination keeps conditional ones lazy). `COALESCE` stops at the first non-NULL argument.

`AND` and `OR` evaluate left to right and short-circuit: `WHERE b <> 0 AND a div b > 1` runs, `WHERE a div b > 1 AND b <> 0` raises `DIVIDE_BY_ZERO` under ANSI. Stacked filters stay in order when the optimizer combines them (`CombineFilters` puts the lower condition first): a filter on `CAST(c AS INT)` above one on `c RLIKE …` runs, and so does a join filter above a guard.

The optimizer pushes a filter below a projection, so `SELECT * FROM (SELECT a div b AS q, b …) WHERE b <> 0` raises on the folded path (the projection runs first on the driver) and runs on the codegen path (the filter moved below the division). That removes raises and adds none.
reference: The reference evaluates an expression only on the rows its operator sees: a `CASE` branch on the rows that reach it, a filter's condition on the rows below it. Its issue analysis trusts that `CASE` is lazy and `AND`/`OR` are not (ST-12). Spark keeps each guard the reference's analysis relies on; its `AND` is lazier than the model assumes.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `if(c2 >= 0, 1-0, 1/0)` over a table with `c2 = 0` rows runs under ANSI: the `1/0` branch is never evaluated
`coalesce(c2, 1/0)` with non-NULL `c2` runs under ANSI: `1/0` is never evaluated
`coalesce(null, 1, 1/0)` is 1.0 under ANSI: evaluation stops at the first non-NULL
`CASE WHEN c2 >= 0 THEN 1 ELSE 1/0 END` over the table runs under ANSI
`CASE WHEN i > 100 THEN 1/0 ELSE 0 END FROM case_tbl` is 0.0 on every row under ANSI

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
